taglines: It's Monday morning and the weekend you were going to use to 'get ahead' is now historical fact. You are not ahead. You are exactly as behind as you were Friday, but now also slightly dehydrated.

The meeting that could have been an email is now a recurring meeting. It has a name. It has a Slack channel. It has outlived three team members and one entire product direction. Nobody knows how to cancel it.

You opened a new tab to look something up, got distracted, opened four more tabs, and now the original question is gone. This is Monday. This is the cognitive environment in which you will make important decisions today.

There is a version of you that wakes up at 5am and journals and does mobility work and has already shipped something meaningful before most people check their phones. That version exists in your mind as a threat, not an inspiration.

Your brain is performing at roughly 60% and you are about to get on a call with someone performing at 90% who will say something reasonable that you will misinterpret as a challenge. Monday is a full-contact sport.

The idea you had in the shower this morning was genuinely good. You thought about it for four minutes, convinced yourself it wouldn't work, and now you're back to doing the same thing you've been doing for six months.

Monday asks: what did you accomplish last week? You respond: I survived it, I maintained most of my relationships, I kept several systems running that would have otherwise failed. Monday nods and says that doesn't count.

The calendar is a work of speculative fiction. It describes a world where you are a different person with better focus, no interruptions, and the ability to teleport between locations. You will spend the week negotiating with it.
